pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: Old Mother Hubbard
work.note: Old Mother Hubbard é uma rima infantil em inglês atribuída a Sarah Catherine Martin e publicada em 1805. Ela conta a história de uma senhora que vai ao armário buscar comida para seu cachorro. A rima segue com várias cenas curtas e bem-humoradas sobre o cão. A rima é mais longa que a maioria, com muitas cenas cômicas. A aula retorna à obra para explorar “dizer quantidade: a lot of (muito), a few (alguns, com plural)

pages.question: Como a história dessa obra ajuda você a imaginar a situação de hoje? Diga uma ideia em inglês.

facts.label: Situação
facts.sub: At a farmers market in San Diego, fruit is sold by the pound or by the box, and the seller often says “That’s eleven dollars.” Learn to buy fruit like a local.

pages.title: Saturday at the market · 1/3
paragraphs: Every Saturday, my friend Lily goes to the farmers market in **San Diego**. The sun is warm, and the fruit is bright. Today I went with her.

We stopped at a table full of apples. “**These apples look good**,” I said. The seller smiled. “**They’re fresh today. Two dollars a pound.**” I said, “**I’ll take three pounds.**” He put the apples on the scale. “**Okay. Anything else?**”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: Saturday at the market · 2/3
paragraphs: “**Do you have strawberries?**” I asked. “**Yes. Five dollars a box.**” “**One box, please.**” “**That’s eleven dollars**,” he said. I paid, and he said, “**Enjoy your fruit!**” Lily laughed. “**What a steal!**” she said.

On my way home, I thought about the old rhyme Old Mother Hubbard. She goes to the cupboard to get a bone for her poor dog, but the cupboard is bare. Our bags were full of fruit, so we were lucky. No bare cupboard for us!

pages.title: Saturday at the market · 3/3
paragraphs: At home, I washed the strawberries and put the apples in a bowl. They were sweet and cold. I think I will go back next Saturday. Shopping at a market is slow, friendly and delicious.

pages.title: Palavras pelo contexto

items.q: They’re fresh today. Two dollars a pound. O que significa “fresh”?
items.why: Fresh = new and not old.

items.q: What a steal! It is very cheap. O que significa “steal”?
items.why: A steal = a very good price.

items.q: He put the apples on the scale. O que significa “scale”?
items.why: A scale shows weight.
